Legend

About these benchmarks

These ten .inp files are the worked examples from the EXTRAN Manual (Roesner, Aldrich & Dickinson) — the dynamic-wave test problems that have validated every EXTRAN and SWMM5 release since the 1980s. The Open Water Analytics project keeps them as its numerical-regression suite.

∂A/∂t + ∂Q/∂x = 0
∂Q/∂t + ∂(Q²/A)/∂x + gA·∂H/∂x + gA·Sf = 0

Every junction shaft is drawn from [JUNCTIONS] invert + max depth; every pipe is extruded as its true cross-section from [XSECTIONS] — egg, horseshoe, arch, box, trapezoid, ellipse and more, not just circles — positioned by [COORDINATES]. Subcatchments come from [SUBCATCHMENTS] + [POLYGONS]. Load the matching .rpt and the viewer colors by results and draws the max-HGL ribbon.

Source: OpenWaterAnalytics/swmm-nrtestsuite

Single-file by design (no build step) on Three.js r128 — the last UMD build cdnjs hosts with everything this app needs; the custom orbit is ~50 lines so artifacts and Netlify behave identically.

Welcome

SWMM5 Benchmark 3D Viewer

See the EPA EXTRAN Manual test networks — the files SWMM5 is regression-tested against on the OWA GitHub — as true 3D models built from their inverts, depths, offsets and cross-sections.

What you can do:
  • Pick any of the 10 benchmarks — tide gate, orifices, weirs, storage, Type 1/2/3 pumps
  • Choose what the labels show — name, invert, length, n, slope, area, % imperv…
  • Pipes render in their real cross-section — egg, horseshoe, arch, box, trapezoid…
  • Click or search any element to inspect its raw .inp parameters
  • Load a SWMM5 .rpt to color by max depth / velocity and draw the max-HGL ribbon
  • Switch to the Sample models in the dropdown — six bigger real networks
  • Or hit GitHub… to browse and load .inp files from any public repo
  • Load a .out file for animated playback — watch depths fill and flow propagate through the storm
  • Drop your own .inp — subcatchment polygons render too — and save PNG / GIF
